articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.
This amendment updates existing authorizations concerning transactions related to Iran, reflecting ongoing adjustments to the sanctions regime.
Further details regarding the scope and specific provisions of the amended general license are available on the OFAC website.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities for North Korea and DRC Activities
body: On October 28, 2026, OFAC announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in North Korea's illicit IT worker schemes and activities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The North Korea designations target 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in government-run IT worker schemes that generate revenue for the DPRK's weapons programs, often by defrauding U.S. businesses through fraudulent documents and stolen identities.
These actions aim to disrupt networks that support the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and address destabilizing activities in the DRC.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking and Rejecting Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026, regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments provide updated guidance and clarifications for financial institutions and other entities on their obligations under OFAC regulations.
The updated FAQs are intended to assist in compliance efforts and ensure proper reporting procedures.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations, and Issues New General Licenses
body: On October 21, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting a Panama- and Greece-based law firm, five individuals, and shipping companies and agents for supporting Iran's shadow fleet and trade in petroleum and petrochemicals.
Concurrently, OFAC removed certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea, indicating a recalibration of sanctions against these countries.
The agency also issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions, providing specific authorizations and clarifications for certain transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations and Associated General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026.
These designations target entities and individuals involved in activities that undermine American intellectual property rights.
Accompanying the designations, OFAC issued associated General Licenses to provide guidance and authorization for certain transactions related to the newly sanctioned parties.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief
body: On October 16, 2026, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and an updated Frequently Asked Question.
This amendment, GL 60A, extends the authorization period for transactions related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela from its original end date of October 23, 2026, to April 21, 2027.
The action aims to facilitate humanitarian assistance in the region.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related and Cuba Designations, Issues New General Licenses
body: On October 15, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation, alongside the issuance of new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions.

The Cuba designation follows the implementation of Executive Order 14404, which established a new Cuba sanctions program targeting non-U.S. companies and foreign banks operating in key sectors of the Cuban economy or supporting the Cuban government.
These actions reflect ongoing efforts to address activities deemed contrary to U.S. foreign policy and national security interests in both Iran and Cuba.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuela-Related Designation
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the removal of a Venezuela-related designation on October 14, 2026.
This action signifies a recalibration of sanctions against Venezuela, potentially indicating a shift in diplomatic engagement or a recognition of changed circumstances.

The delisting of Jorge Rodriguez, President of Venezuela's National Assembly, from the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list ends asset freezes and obstacles for U.S. persons dealing with him.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: On October 13, 2026, OFAC announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These actions are part of a broader strategy to disrupt illicit financial networks that support drug trafficking and terrorist organizations globally.
The designations aim to freeze assets and prevent designated parties from accessing the U.S. financial system.

articles.headline: EU Imposes Largest Russia Sanctions Package to Date, Targets Military-Industrial Complex
body: On October 12, 2026, the Council of the European Union adopted its largest package of Russia-related listings to date, imposing restrictive measures on 1,569 individuals and entities within Russia's military-industrial complex.
The measures cover 826 Russian companies supplying components for missiles, UAVs, and aircraft, as well as 743 individuals serving as CEOs of these companies.
Additionally, the Council listed 77 individuals in connection with the September 2026 Russian State Duma elections held in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine.

articles.headline: EU Adds Individuals and Entities to DPRK Sanctions List Over Nuclear and Missile Programs, Russia Ties
body: The Council of the European Union adopted additional restrictive measures against three individuals and four entities under its autonomous sanctions list on the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) on October 12, 2026.

These designations target those responsible for supporting, promoting, or facilitating activities contributing to the DPRK's nuclear weapons, ballistic missiles, or other weapons of mass destruction programs, as well as for violating and evading United Nations sanctions.

The new listings specifically address activities linked to growing military and economic cooperation between the DPRK and Russia, including the deployment of DPRK workers in Russia and commercial and industrial cooperation.

articles.headline: OFSI Updates UK Sanctions List with Correction for ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida Regime
body: On October 29, 2026, the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office updated the UK Sanctions List on GOV.UK with a correction under the ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida (United Nations Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019.

This administrative amendment involves a correction to an existing entry, with deleted information appearing in strikethrough and red, and newly added information underlined and highlighted in yellow.
The update serves to maintain the accuracy and integrity of the UK's financial sanctions regime.

articles.headline: OFSI Issues New General Licence for Landlord Payments and Amends Gazpromneft-Sakhalin Licence
body: The Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) issued a new General Licence, INT/2026/10050568, on October 12, 2026, permitting designated persons to make payments to UK landlords for ground rent, service charges, and certain late payment fees related to eligible leases in England or Wales.
This new licence took effect on October 12 and is valid until October 11, 2027.

Additionally, OFSI amended General Licence INT/2025/5635700, extending the exemption for business operations with Gazpromneft-Sakhalin LLC and its subsidiaries related to exempt projects until December 31, 2026.

articles.headline: OFSI Issues General Licence for Wind-Down of Transactions with Zarubezhneft JSC
body: The Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) issued General Licence INT/2026/11080040 on October 8, 2026, authorizing the wind-down of transactions involving Zarubezhneft JSC or its subsidiaries.
This licence also covers activities reasonably necessary to complete the wind-down process.
The licence took effect on October 8 and is set to expire on November 21, 2026, providing a limited period for entities to conclude their dealings with the designated Russian company.

articles.headline: President Trump Waives Most Russia Sanctions and Tariffs Under Graham Act
body: On October 16, 2026, President Donald Trump issued an Executive Order waiving the majority of Russia-related sanctions and tariffs introduced by the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026.
The Executive Order invokes Section 115 of the Act, which allows the President to waive sanctions and duties upon certification that such a waiver is in the national interest.
This action effectively returns U.S. Russia-related sanctions to their status quo before the Act's passage, though it does not affect the Iran-related sections of the legislation.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Notice to Foreign Financial Institutions on Iran Business
body: On October 5, 2026, OFAC issued a notice to foreign financial institutions regarding conducting business with Iran.
This advisory highlights the ongoing sanctions risks associated with transactions involving Iran and emphasizes the importance of due diligence for foreign financial institutions.
The notice serves as a reminder of the U.S. government's commitment to enforcing sanctions against Iran and preventing illicit financial activities.

articles.headline: U.S. Sanctions Facilitators of North Korean IT Worker Schemes
body: On October 28, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) government-run information technology (IT) worker schemes.

These schemes allegedly use fraudulent documents, stolen identities, and fabricated personas to obtain employment with legitimate businesses, including in the United States, generating revenue for the DPRK government.

The targeted networks have reportedly used cryptocurrency transactions, money laundering techniques, and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence tools, to generate and transfer funds.

articles.headline: DHS Adds Three Chinese Genomics Companies to UFLPA Entity List
body: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced on October 28, 2026, the addition of three Chinese genomics companies to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List, effective October 29, 2026.

These companies, Shenzhen BGI Technology Co., Ltd. (BGI Group), BGI Genomics Co., Ltd., and MGI Tech Co., Ltd., are affiliated and are considered among the largest advanced gene-sequencing and genetic-material collection enterprises globally.

DHS states that these entities assist the government of the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region in building and operating its mass surveillance infrastructure, and goods produced by them are now subject to a rebuttable presumption of being made with forced labor and are prohibited from entering the United States.

articles.headline: OCC Announces Enforcement Actions, Including $750 Million Penalty Against Bank of America
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released its enforcement actions for October 2026, including a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, National Association, Charlotte, North Carolina.

The penalty against Bank of America addresses significant deficiencies in the bank's Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance program, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and sending wires with inaccurate transmittor name information.

Additionally, the OCC issued a Cease and Desist Order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank, Sandy, Utah, for deficiencies in its BSA compliance program, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and customer due diligence and customer identification program violations.

articles.headline: OCC Issues Prohibition Orders Against Former Bank Employees for Embezzlement
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) issued prohibition orders against two former bank employees in October 2026.

Jennifer Hamblin, a Vault Teller at a Cincinnati, Ohio, branch of Fifth Third Bank, N.A., was prohibited from participating in the affairs of any bank for embezzling approximately $292,000 in customer funds.

Similarly, Christopher Organista, a Former Operations Processor at the La Mirada, California Operations Center of U.S. Bank National Association, Cincinnati, Ohio, received a prohibition order for embezzling approximately $194,131 in bank customer funds.
These actions underscore the OCC's commitment to holding institution-affiliated parties accountable for misconduct.

The additions mean that goods produced by these entities are subject to a rebuttable presumption of being made with forced labor and are prohibited from entering the United States.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.

body: Trump had sued the media outlet after it published a letter to Epstein purportedly written and signed by the president as part of a birthday book.

articles.headline: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials
body: The order comes after election officials received letters demanding they set aside the ballots of possible non-citizen voters.

articles.headline: Alaska Senate candidate denies knowing about alleged plot to put two Dan Sullivans on ballot
body: The incumbent Republican running for re-election and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters by recruiting a second Dan Sullivan to also stand in the race.

articles.headline: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
body: Government data shows that more than 10,000 people have contracted the rare virus.

articles.headline: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
body: The prime minister has previously emphasised military preparedness as central to his government's ambitions.

articles.headline: Spain train disaster clouds Sánchez chances of re-election
body: The Spanish PM is hit by a succession of crises just weeks before a snap general election.

articles.headline: Global nature talks reach deal but money remains an issue
body: Countries have been trying to get a global agreement to halt nature decline back on track.

articles.headline: Police deployed during stand-off over control of top Poland court
body: The escalation came after the government suspended two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them.

articles.headline: Peaceful protests in Germany spiral into violence and looting
body: Thousands joined largely orderly demonstrations earlier in the day, before violence erupted in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.

articles.headline: Watch: Heidi Klum as giant severed hand for Halloween bash
body: The supermodel and TV host provided a gory new shock at her New York event.

articles.headline: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
body: More than 320,000 people demonstrated across France against the rising cost of living and poor public services, with clashes between some protesters and police.

articles.headline: CCTV and zip ties: How US mail-in votes are secured and counted
body: BBC Verify goes to an election centre to get a behind-the-scenes look at how mail-in ballots for the US midterm elections are processed.

articles.headline: Lindsay Clancy is back in court - where will her case go next?
body: The Massachusetts mother, accused of murdering her three children, is expected back in court as she awaits a decision on whether her case will be retried.

articles.headline: Democrats are used to heartbreak in Texas - could Talarico turn the tide?
body: The state's $500m Senate race may be the most closely watched in the US midterms, and is about far more than control of Congress.
